Apply the sine function to both sides of $\sin^{-1}(3x) = -\frac{\pi}{3}$:
$$3x = \sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$

Solve for $x$ in exact radical form:
$$x = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6} \quad \left(\text{or } -\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\right)$$

Factorise the trigonometric equation by grouping terms:
$$2\cos\theta\sin\theta - 2\cos\theta - \sin\theta + 1 = 0$$
$$2\cos\theta(\sin\theta - 1) - 1(\sin\theta - 1) = 0$$
$$(2\cos\theta - 1)(\sin\theta - 1) = 0$$

Find the exact solutions for $\theta$ in the interval $0 \le \theta \le \pi$:
$$\text{From } \cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}: \quad \theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$$
$$\text{From } \sin\theta = 1: \quad \theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } \theta = \frac{\pi}{3}, \quad \frac{\pi}{2})$$
